devPackages.name: fast-check
devPackages.why: Property-based tests in test/property.test.js. Generates inputs for each primitive and shrinks a failure to its smallest case.
devPackages.used: test/property.test.js only. Never imported by src/ or any published entry point.
devPackages.provenance: SLSA provenance on the registry, repository dubzzz/fast-check.

devPackages.name: pure-rand
devPackages.why: The seeded random generator fast-check draws from, so a failing property replays from its seed.
devPackages.provenance: SLSA provenance on the registry, repository dubzzz/pure-rand.

devPackages.name: ajv
devPackages.why: JSON Schema validator. test/cbom.test.js validates the CBOM against the vendored CycloneDX 1.6 schema, and checks that it rejects documents that break the schema.
devPackages.used: test/cbom.test.js only. Never imported by src/, scripts/ or any published entry point.
devPackages.provenance: Registry signature; no SLSA provenance attestation on the registry. Repository ajv-validator/ajv.

devPackages.name: ajv-formats
devPackages.why: The string formats (uri, date-time, email) the CycloneDX schema declares, so the CBOM is validated against them rather than past them.
devPackages.provenance: Registry signature; no SLSA provenance attestation on the registry. Repository ajv-validator/ajv-formats.

devPackages.name: fast-deep-equal
devPackages.why: Deep equality for enum and const keywords inside ajv.
devPackages.provenance: Registry signature; no SLSA provenance attestation on the registry. Repository epoberezkin/fast-deep-equal.

devPackages.name: fast-uri
devPackages.why: URI parsing and resolution for $id and $ref inside ajv.
devPackages.provenance: Registry signature; no SLSA provenance attestation on the registry. Repository fastify/fast-uri.

devPackages.name: json-schema-traverse
devPackages.why: Walks a schema to collect its $id and $ref targets inside ajv.
devPackages.provenance: Registry signature; no SLSA provenance attestation on the registry. Repository epoberezkin/json-schema-traverse.

devPackages.name: require-from-string
devPackages.why: A dependency ajv declares. Only ajv's standalone-code module (ajv/dist/standalone) loads it, and the CBOM test does not load that module.
devPackages.provenance: Registry signature; no SLSA provenance attestation on the registry. Repository floatdrop/require-from-string.

packages.name: @noble/post-quantum
packages.why: The FIPS 203, 204 and 205 primitives. This package is the wrapper around it: parameter-set selection, FIPS 204 context strings, key derivation, fingerprinting and a native backend, none of which change the primitive arithmetic.
packages.auditNote: Self-audited by the maintainer at 0.6.1 in Apr 2026; 0.7.1 is not covered by any audit. No independent audit. This is the reason conformance/ exists in this repository: every parameter set is checked against NIST's own ACVP vectors and cross-checked against liboqs, Bouncy Castle and dilithium-py/kyber-py in both directions, so the primitive is evidenced here rather than taken on the dependency's word.
packages.pinningNote: Pinned exactly, not caret-ranged, so every bump passes the ACVP and interoperability gate. An earlier note said 0.7.1 regressed nine NIST SLH-DSA verify vectors; that was a fault in our ACVP runner, not in 0.7.1.

packages.name: @noble/hashes
packages.why: SHA-256, SHA-512, SHAKE and HKDF. Used for key derivation from a master secret, public-key fingerprinting and the hashes FIPS 205 needs.
packages.externalAudit: Cure53, Jan 2022, at version 1.0.0, funded by the Ethereum Foundation with Nomic Labs. Self-audited at 2.2.0 in Apr 2026.
packages.auditNote: The 2022 Cure53 scope covered everything except blake3, sha3-addons, sha1 and argon2. None of those four are used here.
packages.pinningNote: Pinned exactly and declared directly rather than inherited, so the version this package uses is visible in its own manifest instead of resolved from a transitive range.

packages.name: @noble/curves
packages.why: Reached through @noble/post-quantum, not imported here directly. ml-dsa.js takes `abool` from @noble/curves/utils.js, and _crystals.js, which both ML-DSA and ML-KEM are built on, takes `FFTCore` and `reverseBits` from @noble/curves/abstract/fft.js. So it is on the signing and encapsulation path for every parameter set this package exposes.
packages.externalAudit: Trail of Bits, Feb 2023, at 0.7.3. Kudelski Security, Sep 2023, at 1.2.0. Cure53, Sep 2024, at 1.6.0. Self-audited at 2.2.0 in Apr 2026.
packages.auditNote: The most heavily reviewed package in the tree, and it is on the hot path rather than idle in it. Three independent firms across four years: Trail of Bits, Kudelski Security and Cure53. The reachability check in run-audit.mjs established this rather than the manifest: nothing in this package's own source names @noble/curves.
packages.pinningNote: Resolved from @noble/post-quantum 0.7.1's exact 2.4.0 requirement and locked in package-lock.json.

packages.name: @noble/ciphers
packages.why: Not used by this package. Transitive dependency of @noble/post-quantum.
packages.externalAudit: Cure53, Sep 2024, at version 1.0.0, funded by OpenSats. Self-audited at 2.2.0 in Apr 2026.
packages.auditNote: Present but not reachable from this package's published surface.
packages.pinningNote: Resolved from @noble/post-quantum 0.7.1's exact 2.4.0 requirement and locked in package-lock.json.
